title: plan compute capacity before a forecasted workload increase
input: The platform owner selects the supported fleet, utilization evidence and required growth assumptions.
action: Capacity Planner presents supported capacity-planning information for the chosen workload scope. Planning output informs reservation or provisioning decisions; it does not itself execute application jobs or guarantee every forecasted resource.
output: The owner provisions the approved capacity through the actual compute administration workflow.
check: Compare forecast assumptions, real utilization and available capacity before accepting the scale plan.

title: control employee access to a protected web application
input: The employee uses the managed browser and requests an assigned enterprise application.
action: Chrome Enterprise Premium's configured browser and access-security capabilities evaluate supported device, user and content controls. The protected application still validates its own business permissions and resource ownership.
output: The employee uses the approved web application under the effective browser and access policy.
check: Test unmanaged devices, denied users, download restrictions and the actual integrating access enforcement configuration.

title: associate a project with an approved billing account
input: The finance owner selects the correct project, billing account and authorized billing roles.
action: Cloud Billing records the supported account-to-project billing relationship and exposes billing or cost information. Linking enables eligible resource charging; budgets provide notifications rather than a guaranteed universal spending stop.
output: The project owner deploys only approved resources and the finance team tracks their actual charges.
check: Verify billing-account permissions, project linkage, data delay and resource costs before accepting the allocation.

title: develop and test a Cloud Run service through supported IDE tools
input: The developer selects an approved repository and supported Cloud Code environment.
action: Cloud Code integrates supported cloud development workflows into the IDE, such as local debugging and deployment assistance. Build and deployment tools execute the actual commands using their configured credentials.
output: The developer validates the API locally and promotes the reviewed image through the project release pipeline.
check: Check deployment project, runtime identity, local-versus-cloud configuration and acceptance tests before release.

title: register a permitted application domain and configure its DNS
input: The domain owner selects an available name, authorized contact details and the intended DNS provider.
action: Cloud Domains coordinates supported domain-registration and management operations. The chosen DNS service publishes records, while the application's hosting endpoint serves traffic; domain registration does not create that backend.
output: The site owner publishes the verified DNS records and completes the endpoint's HTTPS configuration.
check: Check ownership, renewal, authoritative DNS resolution and certificate hostname before opening the website.

title: inspect an application's resource state and assigned operations context
input: The operator selects the permitted application resources and the operational question.
action: Cloud Hub presents supported centralized resource and operational information. The operator examines the actual resource evidence and navigates to the responsible service; the hub does not replace application execution or source-service controls.
output: The owner investigates the affected resource and records its verified operational action.
check: Check scope, data freshness and actual service state before accepting a displayed summary as incident evidence.

title: grant an employee group the approved cloud role
input: The identity owner defines the employee account, group membership and role approval.
action: Cloud Identity manages supported organizational identities and groups. The resource IAM policy grants a selected role to the group; identity membership and IAM authorization are separate configured layers.
output: The employee signs in and performs only the operations permitted by the effective group-based IAM grants.
check: Test membership removal, federation configuration and denied-resource access before accepting onboarding or offboarding.

title: select a supported deployment location meeting workload constraints
input: The architect defines location requirements, supported cloud provider scope and the application's geographic constraints.
action: Cloud Location Finder supplies supported cloud-location information for comparison and selection. The architect checks the chosen location's actual services and requirements; location discovery does not provision infrastructure.
output: The deployment owner creates resources in the reviewed location through its actual provider APIs.
check: Verify service availability, latency assumptions and data-location requirements before accepting the selected Region.

title: procure a reviewed partner application for the cloud estate
input: The buyer evaluates the vendor offer, licensing scope and deployment prerequisites.
action: Marketplace supports procurement and entitlement for the selected partner product. The approved subscription or offer enables its use; the vendor software still requires the configured deployment and operational responsibility.
output: The platform owner deploys the entitled application with reviewed network and identity settings.
check: Check entitlement, vendor support, infrastructure costs and actual application behavior before accepting procurement as deployment completion.

title: request required quota before a controlled capacity increase
input: The platform owner identifies the service, quota dimension, project and desired deployment capacity.
action: Cloud Quotas exposes supported quota information and adjustment workflows. A granted quota permits resource requests within that limit; it does not guarantee physical capacity or automatically deploy the workload.
output: The deployment owner provisions the approved capacity and handles actual availability errors separately.
check: Check effective project and regional limits, request status and successful deployment before accepting the scale plan.
